forcedChoices.choice: Commandments 1 to 7 use the second person singular (tú: «No servirás», «No matarás»).
forcedChoices.reason: Each commandment addresses each believer; Spanish forces singular or plural, and the context supports the individual.
The invitation addresses two brothers, so the plural ustedes is required.
Melchizedek speaks to one person, Abraham.
Order of beings is masculine «orden» in Spanish, as in the earlier glossary («orden de los Días»).
The English unit is kept; a conversion to meters would add precision the text does not give.

forcedChoices.choice: «nacía en deuda con los dioses» for "born under forfeit to the gods"
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish has no direct equivalent of "under forfeit"; «en deuda» keeps the sense of an obligation owed from birth.
